blind_spots.note: Attribution stops at the assembled text: the plugin can prove a fusion happened but cannot prove whether the relay or the adapter assigned one index to two calls.

Closed 2026-11-09: P-0001 was verified on a real headless DSH profile (remedy-live, dsh 0.2.2-rc.1). Evidence: data/results/live-2026-11-09T17-00-00.000Z.json. The desktop profile was not restarted; that remains the next mount.
The plugin journal is off by default. A repair that happens in a session with no journal leaves only the session log as evidence.
Synthetic ids are deterministic per call but not stable across replays; they are traceability aids, not durable identities.
The message fallback parses `Received arguments:` from the adapter's English failure text. A localized host message would disable that fallback; the delta buffer path still works.
A max-tokens truncation is never repaired: the tail is missing, and inventing it would dispatch a call the model did not make.

The live headless profile does not persist assistant/attempt streams, so the artifact's session.fused_calls is 0 even on a repaired turn. The repair is evidenced by the journal counters and the synthetic tool-call id; a profile that logs attempts would make the two agree.

Closed 2026-11-09: dsh-remedy was mounted on the desktop profile, the app was restarted, and the desktop process repaired 2 fused calls across 39 streams (data/results/live-desktop-2026-11-09T19-10-00.000Z.json). The tarball sha256 is still what the evidence covers.

The desktop journal covers the whole app process, so its 2 repaired calls span two sessions while the attached session file shows 1. The artifact records journal_scope explicitly; a per-session journal would make the two agree.

Registry copies lag the publish call by seconds. publish-2026-11-10T00-10-00.000Z.json is red because it was recorded at 06:35:37Z and the 0.1.1 copy appeared at 06:35:35Z in the packument but not in the view used by the check. Red publish artifacts are kept and a new stamp records the settled state.
